title: HEVC in MP4: why won't it play on my iPhone / Safari? (hvc1 vs hev1)
fullTitle: FFmpeg HEVC in MP4: -tag:v hvc1 Retags Without Touching a Frame

scenes.narration: Your H E V C file in M P4 will not play on an iPhone or in Safari. The advice: ffmpeg writes h e v one, Apple wants h v c one, so add dash tag colon v, h v c one. We measure what ffmpeg writes and what the flag changes. We cannot test an Apple player.
captions: libx265 to MP4: hev1 or hvc1?

scenes.narration: The source is a synthetic test pattern: fifty frames, encoded with lib x two six five. Reader one is f f probe, reading the codec tag. Reader two is a raw M P4 box parse: the sample entry in s t s d, and the h v c C box. Reader three is the stream: packet and frame hashes. The control: a file written with each tag.
captions: 50 frames. ffprobe tag, raw stsd, stream hashes.
Control: files written with hev1 and hvc1.

scenes.narration: With no tag, ffmpeg writes h e v one. F f probe says h e v one. The raw box says h e v one, with an h v c C box inside. A copy to mov, and from Matroska to M P4, give h e v one too. Asking for h e v one explicitly gives byte for byte the same file.
captions: mp4, mov, mkv to mp4: all hev1.

scenes.narration: Now dash c copy, dash tag colon v, h v c one. Both readers say h v c one. The packets, the raw samples and the decoded frames all hash the same. Zero of fifty frames change. Against a plain copy, every byte that differs is inside the sample entry.

How big is the label change? It depends on the build. On ffmpeg six point one point one, the retag rewrites two bytes. On eight point one point two, it also sets the parameter set flags: five bytes. A plain copy changes none on six. On eight it fills in the average bitrate: three bytes in the bitrate box, also in the sample entry.
captions: Plain copy vs encode: 0 and 3 bytes.

scenes.narration: So the tag is a label. A stream with parameter sets inside its first sample keeps them under h v c one: the retag checks nothing. Matroska has no such tag. Not tested: any Apple player, other builds, other encoders, hardware encoders, real footage.
captions: Not tested: Apple players, real footage.
